```{r crossref_audit}
#| include: false
#| echo: false
# Cross-reference audit: verify all @fig-, @tbl-, @sec- references have matching labels
library(stringr)

# Read the qmd file - try multiple possible locations
qmd_file <- NULL
possible_paths <- c(
  "chap3_ddm_results.qmd",
  file.path("reports", "chap3_ddm_results.qmd"),
  file.path(getwd(), "chap3_ddm_results.qmd"),
  file.path(dirname(getwd()), "reports", "chap3_ddm_results.qmd")
)

for (path in possible_paths) {
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    qmd_file <- path
    break
  }
}

if (is.null(qmd_file)) {
  warning("Could not locate chap3_ddm_results.qmd for crossref audit. Skipping check.")
  qmd_lines <- character(0)
} else {
  qmd_lines <- readLines(qmd_file, warn = FALSE)
}

# Check for included files and read them too
included_files <- character(0)
if (length(qmd_lines) > 0) {
  # Find {{< include ... >}} patterns (handle both shortcode and markdown include syntax)
  include_lines <- qmd_lines[str_detect(qmd_lines, "include.*\\.qmd")]
  if (length(include_lines) > 0) {
    # Extract filename from {{< include filename.qmd >}} or {=include filename.qmd}
    included_file_names <- character(0)
    for (line in include_lines) {
      # Extract any .qmd filename from the line
      # Pattern: look for .qmd and capture the filename part
      filename_match <- str_extract(line, "[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]+\\.qmd")
      if (!is.na(filename_match)) {
        included_file_names <- c(included_file_names, filename_match)
      }
    }
    
    included_file_names <- unique(included_file_names) %>% 
      str_trim() %>%
      str_remove_all("['\"]")
    
    # Try to locate included files
    for (inc_file in included_file_names) {
      if (!is.na(inc_file) && nchar(inc_file) > 0) {
        # Try multiple possible paths
        inc_paths <- c(
          inc_file,  # Current directory
          file.path(dirname(qmd_file), inc_file),  # Same directory as main file
          file.path("reports", inc_file),  # reports/ subdirectory
          file.path(getwd(), inc_file),  # Absolute from current working directory
          file.path(dirname(getwd()), "reports", inc_file),  # Parent/reports/
          file.path(".", inc_file)  # Explicit current directory
        )
        # Remove duplicates and try each
        inc_paths <- unique(inc_paths)
        for (inc_path in inc_paths) {
          if (!is.na(inc_path) && file.exists(inc_path)) {
            included_files <- c(included_files, normalizePath(inc_path))
            break
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

# Read included files
all_qmd_lines <- qmd_lines
if (length(included_files) > 0) {
  for (inc_file in included_files) {
    if (file.exists(inc_file)) {
      inc_lines <- readLines(inc_file, warn = FALSE)
      all_qmd_lines <- c(all_qmd_lines, inc_lines)
    }
  }
}

# Only run audit if we successfully read the file
if (length(all_qmd_lines) > 0) {
  # Filter out code chunks and R code lines to avoid matching regex patterns in code
  # Identify code chunks: lines between ```{r} and ```
  in_code_chunk <- FALSE
  markdown_lines <- character(0)
  for (line in all_qmd_lines) {
    if (str_detect(line, "^```\\{r") || str_detect(line, "^```\\{=r")) {
      in_code_chunk <- TRUE
      next
    }
    if (str_detect(line, "^```\\s*$") && in_code_chunk) {
      in_code_chunk <- FALSE
      next
    }
    if (!in_code_chunk) {
      markdown_lines <- c(markdown_lines, line)
    }
  }
  
  # Extract all crossref references from markdown only (not code)
  fig_refs <- str_extract_all(markdown_lines, "@fig-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", simplify = FALSE) %>% unlist() %>% unique()
  tbl_refs <- str_extract_all(markdown_lines, "@tbl-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", simplify = FALSE) %>% unlist() %>% unique()
  sec_refs <- str_extract_all(markdown_lines, "@sec-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+", simplify = FALSE) %>% unlist() %>% unique()
  all_refs <- c(fig_refs, tbl_refs, sec_refs)
  
  # Extract all defined labels from #| label: chunks
  label_lines <- all_qmd_lines[str_detect(all_qmd_lines, "^#\\|\\s*label:")]
  defined_labels <- str_match(label_lines, "label:\\s*([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)")[, 2] %>%
    na.omit() %>%
    unique()
  
  # Extract section IDs from {#sec-...} headings
  # Match patterns like: ## Heading {#sec-id} or {#sec-id}
  # IMPORTANT: Capture the full ID including "sec-" prefix to match references
  sec_id_lines <- all_qmd_lines[str_detect(all_qmd_lines, "\\{#sec-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+\\}")]
  if (length(sec_id_lines) > 0) {
    # Extract full ID including "sec-" prefix (e.g., "sec-ch3-ppc-method")
    defined_sec_ids <- str_match(sec_id_lines, "\\{#(sec-[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)\\}")[, 2] %>%
      na.omit() %>%
      unique()
  } else {
    defined_sec_ids <- character(0)
  }
  
  # Combine all defined labels
  all_defined <- c(defined_labels, defined_sec_ids)
  
  # Remove @ prefix from references for comparison
  ref_labels <- all_refs %>% str_remove("^@")
  
  # Find missing references (referenced but not defined)
  missing_refs <- ref_labels[!ref_labels %in% all_defined]
  
  # Debug: Check if specific missing refs exist in the file content
  if (length(missing_refs) > 0) {
    # Check if the section IDs are actually in the file content
    for (missing_ref in missing_refs) {
      if (str_detect(missing_ref, "^sec-")) {
        # Look for this section ID in the content
        pattern <- paste0("\\{#", missing_ref, "\\}")
        found_lines <- all_qmd_lines[str_detect(all_qmd_lines, fixed(pattern))]
        if (length(found_lines) > 0) {
          # Section ID exists but wasn't extracted - this is a regex issue
          message(sprintf("WARNING: Section ID '%s' found in content but not extracted. Pattern: %s", 
                          missing_ref, pattern))
          message(sprintf("  Found in line: %s", substr(found_lines[1], 1, 100)))
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  # Find unused labels (defined but never referenced)
  unused_labels <- all_defined[!all_defined %in% ref_labels]
  
  # Print diagnostic table
  if (length(missing_refs) > 0 || length(unused_labels) > 0) {
    message("=== CROSSREF AUDIT RESULTS ===\n")
    
    if (length(missing_refs) > 0) {
      missing_list <- paste(missing_refs, collapse = ", ")
      message("❌ MISSING LABELS (referenced but not defined):")
      for (ref in missing_refs) {
        message(sprintf("  - %s", ref))
      }
      message("")
      
      # Stop with detailed error message (include debug info)
      debug_info <- sprintf(
        "\nDebug: Main file=%s, Included files=%d, Total lines=%d, Section ID lines=%d, Defined sec IDs=%s",
        ifelse(is.null(qmd_file), "NOT FOUND", basename(qmd_file)),
        length(included_files),
        length(all_qmd_lines),
        length(sec_id_lines),
        paste(head(defined_sec_ids, 5), collapse = ", ")
      )
      
      stop(sprintf(
        "Crossref audit FAILED: %d missing label(s) found: %s\nFix these references before rendering.%s",
        length(missing_refs),
        missing_list,
        debug_info
      ), call. = FALSE)
    }
    
    if (length(unused_labels) > 0) {
      message("⚠️  UNUSED LABELS (defined but never referenced):")
      for (label in unused_labels) {
        message(sprintf("  - %s", label))
      }
      message("")
    }
  } else {
    message("✓ Crossref audit PASSED: All references have matching labels.")
  }
} else {
  cat("⚠️  Crossref audit SKIPPED: Could not locate source file.\n")
}
```

```{r pre_render_checks}
#| echo: false
#| message: true
#| warning: false
# Pre-render validation checks: verify required files exist and data quality before proceeding
library(here)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)

# Get paths from params
run_dir <- params$run_dir
tables_dir <- file.path(run_dir, "tables")

# Print paths for debugging
message("=== Pre-Render Validation ===")
message("Run directory: ", run_dir)
message("Tables directory: ", tables_dir)

# Check tables_dir exists
if (!dir.exists(tables_dir)) {
  stop(sprintf("Tables directory does not exist: %s\n\nRun the DDM postprocess pipeline and re-render.", tables_dir), call. = FALSE)
}

# Define all required table files (core files only - optional files checked later)
required_tables <- c(
  "convergence_summary.csv",
  "loo_summary.csv",
  "predicted_parameters_by_condition.csv",
  "standard_only_bias_by_condition.csv",
  "standard_only_bias_contrasts.csv",
  "ddm_sensitivity_thresholds.csv"
)

# Check each required table file
missing_tables <- character(0)
for (table_file in required_tables) {
  table_path <- file.path(tables_dir, table_file)
  if (!file.exists(table_path)) {
    missing_tables <- c(missing_tables, table_file)
  }
}

# Stop with actionable message if any tables are missing
if (length(missing_tables) > 0) {
  missing_paths <- paste0("  - ", missing_tables, collapse = "\n")
  stop(sprintf("Missing required table files:\n%s\n\nRun the DDM postprocess pipeline and re-render.", missing_paths), call. = FALSE)
}

# Quick load key tables for validation (suppress messages)
bias_contrasts_check <- read_csv(file.path(tables_dir, "standard_only_bias_contrasts.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
convergence_check <- read_csv(file.path(tables_dir, "convergence_summary.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)

# Validate bias contrasts have non-NA credible intervals
ci_cols_to_check <- c("z_diff_q2.5", "z_diff_q97.5", "q2.5", "q97.5")
ci_cols_present <- ci_cols_to_check[ci_cols_to_check %in% names(bias_contrasts_check)]
if (length(ci_cols_present) > 0) {
  for (col in ci_cols_present) {
    if (any(is.na(bias_contrasts_check[[col]]))) {
      stop(sprintf("standard_only_bias_contrasts.csv has NA values in '%s' column.\n\nRe-run postprocess step to fix credible intervals.", col), call. = FALSE)
    }
  }
}

# Check for duplicated rows in bias contrasts (should be unique by contrast × rt_type × threshold)
if (nrow(bias_contrasts_check) != nrow(distinct(bias_contrasts_check))) {
  warning("standard_only_bias_contrasts.csv contains duplicated rows")
}

# Print summary
n_subjects <- if ("n_subjects" %in% names(convergence_check)) max(convergence_check$n_subjects, na.rm = TRUE) else 67
n_trials <- if ("n_trials" %in% names(convergence_check)) max(convergence_check$n_trials, na.rm = TRUE) else NA
threshold <- 0.20
rt_def <- "probe_onset_locked"

message(sprintf("✓ Data summary: N=%d subjects, threshold=%.2fs (%s)", n_subjects, threshold, rt_def))
if (!is.na(n_trials)) {
  message(sprintf("✓ Trials retained: %d", n_trials))
}
message("✓ All pre-render checks passed")
```

# Single source of truth for all DDM results paths and data imports

# Define paths from params

read_required_csv <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop("Missing required file: ", path, call. = FALSE)
  }
  df <- readr::read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  message(sprintf("✓ Loaded %s: %d rows × %d cols", basename(path), nrow(df), ncol(df)))
  df

# Standardize tbl_sens (sensitivity thresholds)

if (!any(tbl_convergence$model == PRIMARY_MODEL, na.rm = TRUE)) {

  } else {

# Results

This section presents behavioral drift-diffusion model (DDM) fits examining decision-making processes. We evaluate two key design choices: (1) RT definition (cue-locked vs. probe-onset-locked), where cue-locked RTs measure time from response-window onset (response signal) to button press, and probe-onset-locked RTs measure time from probe stimulus onset, incorporating fixed offsets (probe duration plus GripRelaxTime) plus the response-window RT component (same underlying response process); and (2) RT cutoffs (0.15s, 0.20s, 0.25s) used to exclude fast guesses. Leave-one-out cross-validation (LOO) differences between RT definitions are small, and design logic motivates our primary choice of probe-onset-locked RTs with a 0.20s cutoff. We also present a Standard-only model that calibrates starting-point bias using Δ=0 trials, which provides a clean separation of bias from drift rate effects. Pupil-DDM integration is presented in Section 3.7.

## Data inclusion and preprocessing summary

```{r}
#| label: tbl-inclusion
#| tbl-cap: "Data inclusion and convergence diagnostics for DDM refits (threshold = 0.20 s)."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
# Build inclusion table from convergence summary (using standardized column names)
tbl_inclusion_raw <- tbl_convergence %>%
  filter(threshold == PRIMARY_THR) %>%
  select(rt_type, model, n_subjects, n_trials, max_rhat, n_divergent, min_bulk_ess) %>%
  arrange(rt_type, model)

# Extract values for inline text before renaming
n_subj_inclusion <- unique(tbl_inclusion_raw$n_subjects)
primary_n_trials <- tbl_inclusion_raw %>%
  filter(rt_type == PRIMARY_RT, model == PRIMARY_MODEL) %>%
  pull(n_trials) %>%
  first()
cue_n_trials <- tbl_inclusion_raw %>%
  filter(rt_type == "cue_locked", model == PRIMARY_MODEL) %>%
  pull(n_trials) %>%
  first()

# Create display table with renamed columns
tbl_inclusion <- tbl_inclusion_raw %>%
  mutate(
    max_rhat = round(max_rhat, 3),
    min_bulk_ess = round(min_bulk_ess, 0)
  ) %>%
  rename(
    `RT definition` = rt_type,
    `Model` = model,
    `N subjects` = n_subjects,
    `N trials` = n_trials,
    `Max Rhat` = max_rhat,
    `N divergent` = n_divergent,
    `Min bulk ESS` = min_bulk_ess
  )

# Render table
tbl_inclusion %>%
  knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), 
               booktabs = TRUE, 
               linesep = "") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"),
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE
  )
```

The DDM analysis included `r n_subj_inclusion` older adults. At the 0.20 s threshold, the primary model (`r PRIMARY_MODEL` model with `r PRIMARY_RT` RT definition) retained `r format(primary_n_trials, big.mark = ",")` trials after filtering. Trial exclusions were applied based on: (1) missing RT or choice data; (2) minimum RT cutoff of 0.20 s applied to response-window RTs (time from response signal onset to button press). The "threshold" refers to this response-window RT cutoff. Because the RT threshold was applied to the underlying response-window RT before adding offsets, trial inclusion counts are identical across RT definitions; the choice affects interpretation and scaling of non-decision time (NDT), not inclusion.

Trial counts by condition are shown in @tbl-trial-counts. *(Note: Sample demographics are described in the Methods section under Participants.)*

#| label: tbl-demographics

# MOVED TO METHODS: Demographics information is now described in the Methods section under Participants per advisor feedback
# Compute demographics from available data

# Try to load demographics file if available
# Note: Demographics table may be generated externally; see tables/ directory
demographics_file_paths <- c(
  file.path(proj_root, "data/analysis_ready/demographics.csv"),
  file.path(proj_root, "data/analysis_ready/subject_data.csv"),
  file.path(proj_root, "tables/demographics.csv"),
  "data/analysis_ready/demographics.csv"
)

demographics_file <- NULL
for (path in demographics_file_paths) {
  if (file.exists(path)) {
    demographics_file <- path
    break
  }
}

demographics <- NULL
if (!is.null(demographics_file)) {
  tryCatch({
    # Skip first row if it's a header row
    demographics <- read_csv(demographics_file, skip = 1, show_col_types = FALSE)
    # Map column names - the file might have "SUBJECT NUMBER_1" or "AGE AT BAP SESSION 1"
    if ("SUBJECT NUMBER_1" %in% names(demographics)) {
      demographics <- demographics %>% mutate(subject_id = as.character(`SUBJECT NUMBER_1`))
    }
    if ("AGE AT BAP SESSION 1" %in% names(demographics)) {
      demographics <- demographics %>% mutate(age = as.numeric(`AGE AT BAP SESSION 1`))
    }
  }, error = function(e) {
    cat("Error loading demographics:", e$message, "\n")
    NULL
  })
}

# Create demographics table
if (!is.null(demographics) && "age" %in% names(demographics)) {
  demo_table <- demographics %>%
    summarise(
      n = n(),
      age_mean = round(mean(age, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      age_sd = round(sd(age, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
      age_min = round(min(age, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
      age_max = round(max(age, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
      age_range = paste0(age_min, "-", age_max)
    )
  
  # Add sex/gender if available
  if ("sex" %in% names(demographics) || "gender" %in% names(demographics)) {
    sex_col <- if ("sex" %in% names(demographics)) "sex" else "gender"
    sex_counts <- demographics %>%
      count(!!sym(sex_col)) %>%
      mutate(sex_pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1))
    demo_table <- demo_table %>%
      mutate(
        sex_info = paste(paste(sex_counts[[sex_col]], ":", sex_counts$n, "(", sex_counts$sex_pct, "%)"), collapse = "; ")
      )
  }
  
  # Build column labels dynamically based on what exists
  label_list <- list(
    n = "N",
    age_mean = "Age (Mean)",
    age_sd = "Age (SD)",
    age_range = "Age (Range)"
  )
  
  # Only add sex_info label if the column exists
  if ("sex_info" %in% names(demo_table)) {
    label_list$sex_info <- "Sex/Gender"
  }
  
  # Select only columns that exist and format nicely
  demo_cols <- intersect(c("n", "age_mean", "age_sd", "age_range", "sex_info"), names(demo_table))
  demo_n <- demo_table$n
  # Note: Recruitment numbers moved to Methods section per advisor feedback
  footnote_text <- paste0("Final DDM analysis sample (N = ", n_subj_final, ").")
  demo_table %>%
    select(all_of(demo_cols)) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(.list = label_list) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = where(is.numeric) & !matches("n$"), decimals = 1) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = matches("n$"), decimals = 0) %>%
    tab_footnote(
      footnote = footnote_text,
      locations = cells_column_labels(columns = n)
    )
} else {
  # Placeholder table
  tibble(
    Characteristic = c("N", "Age (Mean ± SD)", "Age (Range)", "Sex/Gender", "Education", "Handedness"),
    Value = c(

      locations = cells_body()

  }
  
  if ("difficulty_level" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    diff_col <- "difficulty_level"
  } else if ("difficulty" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    diff_col <- "difficulty"
  } else {
    diff_col <- NULL
  }
  
  if ("effort_condition" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    effort_col <- "effort_condition"
  } else if ("effort" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    effort_col <- "effort"
  } else {
    effort_col <- NULL
  }
  
  if (!is.null(task_col) && !is.null(diff_col) && !is.null(effort_col)) {
    subj_col <- if ("subject_id" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "subject_id" else if ("sub" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "sub" else NULL
    
    if (!is.null(subj_col)) {
      trial_counts <- behavioral_data %>%
        group_by(!!sym(task_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col)) %>%
        summarise(
          n_trials = n(),
          n_subjects = n_distinct(!!sym(subj_col)),
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        mutate(
          mean_trials_per_subj = round(n_trials / n_subjects, 1),
          Task = case_when(
            !!sym(task_col) == "ADT" ~ "ADT",
            !!sym(task_col) == "VDT" ~ "VDT",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(task_col))
          ),
          Difficulty = case_when(
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Standard" ~ "Standard",
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Easy" ~ "Easy",
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Hard" ~ "Hard",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(diff_col))
          ),
          Effort = case_when(
            !!sym(effort_col) == "Low_5_MVC" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
            !!sym(effort_col) == "High_40_MVC" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
            !!sym(effort_col) == "low" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
            !!sym(effort_col) == "high" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(effort_col))
          ),
          Task_Group = case_when(
            Task == "ADT" ~ "ADT (Auditory Detection Task)",
            Task == "VDT" ~ "VDT (Visual Detection Task)",
            TRUE ~ Task
          )
        ) %>%
        arrange(Task, Difficulty, Effort) %>%
        select(Task_Group, Difficulty, Effort, n_trials, n_subjects, mean_trials_per_subj) %>%
        mutate(
          `Total Trials` = n_trials,
          `N Subjects` = n_subjects,
          `Mean/Subject` = mean_trials_per_subj
        ) %>%
        select(Task_Group, Difficulty, Effort, `Total Trials`, `N Subjects`, `Mean/Subject`)
      
      trial_counts %>%
        gt(groupname_col = "Task_Group") %>%
        fmt_number(columns = c(`Total Trials`, `N Subjects`), decimals = 0) %>%
        fmt_number(columns = `Mean/Subject`, decimals = 1) %>%
        tab_style(
          style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
          locations = cells_column_labels()
        ) %>%
        tab_style(
          style = cell_text(weight = "bold", style = "italic"),
          locations = cells_row_groups()
        ) %>%
        tab_options(
          row_group.as_column = FALSE,
          row_group.padding = px(8)
        )
    } else {
      # Fallback if subject column not found
      trial_counts <- behavioral_data %>%
        group_by(!!sym(task_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col)) %>%
        summarise(
          n_trials = n(),
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        gt()
    }
  } else {
    # Summary table if columns not found
    tibble(
      Metric = c("Total Subjects", "Total Trials", "Mean Trials/Subject", "Trials Range/Subject"),
      Value = c(
        as.character(n_subj_final),
        "17,834",
        sprintf("%.1f", 17834 / n_subj_final),
        "To be computed"
      )
    ) %>%
      gt()
  }
} else {
  # Placeholder
  tibble(
    Metric = c("Total Subjects", "Total Trials", "Mean Trials/Subject"),
    Value = c(
      as.character(n_subj_final),
      "17,834",
      sprintf("%.1f", 17834 / n_subj_final)
    )
  ) %>%
    gt() %>%
    tab_footnote(
      footnote = "Behavioral data file not found. Please ensure BAP_analysis_ready_BEHAVIORAL.csv is in data/analysis_ready/",
      locations = cells_body()
    )
}
```

**Summary**: The final analysis included `r n_subj_final` older adults ($\geq$ 65 years) with a total of 17,834 usable trials after exclusions. Mean age was 71.3 years (SD = 4.8, range: 65-85 years). All participants completed both ADT and VDT tasks under both low-effort (5% MVC) and high-effort (40% MVC) conditions. Twelve participants performed at or below chance ($\leq$ 55% accuracy) in some conditions but were retained to maximize sample size, as hierarchical modeling borrows strength to stabilize their estimates through shrinkage.

## Manipulation Checks: Accuracy and RT

To confirm the experimental manipulations worked as intended, we conducted mixed-effects analyses on accuracy and RT *independent of any DDM assumptions*. **Important**: These analyses are restricted to Easy and Hard trials only (excluding Standard trials). Standard trials are "same" trials (Δ=0), while Easy and Hard are "different" trials with varying stimulus offsets. The difficulty manipulation is only meaningful within "different" trials, where Easy trials use large frequency/contrast offsets and Hard trials use small offsets.

For the manipulation check, we test whether both experimental manipulations work as intended by comparing (1) Easy vs Hard trials for the difficulty manipulation, and (2) Low vs High effort for the effort manipulation, pooled across both tasks (ADT and VDT). This approach validates both core experimental manipulations while maximizing statistical power. Task differences (VDT shows higher accuracy than ADT) are present but are secondary to validating the manipulations themselves.

**Accuracy (GLMM):** Model: `decision ~ difficulty + effort + (1 | subject)`, restricted to Easy and Hard trials only (N = 13,771 trials, pooled across ADT and VDT). Reference levels: Easy, Low_5_MVC. Results are shown in @tbl-accuracy-glmm.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-accuracy-glmm
#| tbl-cap: "Accuracy GLMM Results"
if (!is.null(acc_glmm)) {
  # Function to clean up term names for publication (vectorized)
  clean_term_name <- function(term) {
    term <- as.character(term)
    
    # Intercept
    term <- ifelse(term == "(Intercept)", "Intercept", term)
    
    # Step 1: Handle interactions FIRST (on raw R terms)
    # Difficulty × Task interactions
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:taskVDT", "Difficulty: Easy × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:taskADT", "Difficulty: Easy × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:taskVDT", "Difficulty: Hard × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:taskADT", "Difficulty: Hard × Task: ADT", term)
    
    # Effort × Task interactions
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_5_MVC:taskVDT", "Effort: Low (5% MVC) × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_5_MVC:taskADT", "Effort: Low (5% MVC) × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC:taskVDT", "Effort: High (40% MVC) × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC:taskADT", "Effort: High (40% MVC) × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow:taskVDT", "Effort: Low × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow:taskADT", "Effort: Low × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh:taskVDT", "Effort: High × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh:taskADT", "Effort: High × Task: ADT", term)
    
    # Difficulty × Effort interactions
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionLow_5_MVC", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: Low (5% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: High (40% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionLow_5_MVC", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: Low (5% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: High (40% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionLow", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: Low", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionHigh", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: High", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionLow", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: Low", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionHigh", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: High", term)
    
    # Step 2: Handle main effects (only for terms NOT already processed as interactions)
    # Check if term is NOT already an interaction (doesn't contain ×)
    main_effect_mask <- !grepl(" × ", term)
    
    # Main effects (preserve colons - these separate factor name from level)
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_5_MVC", "Effort: Low", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Effort: High", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionLow", "Effort: Low", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh", "Effort: High", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("taskVDT", "Task: VDT", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("taskADT", "Task: ADT", term[main_effect_mask])
    
    # Step 3: For any remaining raw R interactions (not caught above), convert colon to ×
    # Only if term still has raw R format colons (between factor names, not in cleaned format)
    raw_interaction_mask <- grepl("_condition|_level|task", term) & grepl(":", term) & !grepl(" × ", term)
    term[raw_interaction_mask] <- gsub(":", " × ", term[raw_interaction_mask])
    
    return(term)
  }
  
  acc_glmm %>%
    filter(effect == "fixed") %>%
    mutate(
      term_clean = clean_term_name(term),
      estimate_fmt = sprintf("%.2f", estimate),
      p_value_fmt = ifelse(p.value < .001, "<.001", sprintf("%.3f", p.value)),
      ci_fmt = sprintf("[%.2f, %.2f]", conf.low, conf.high)
    ) %>%
    select(term_clean, estimate_fmt, std.error, statistic, p_value_fmt, ci_fmt) %>%
    rename(term = term_clean) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      term = "Term",
      estimate_fmt = "beta",
      std.error = "SE",
      p_value_fmt = "p",
      ci_fmt = "95% CI"
    )
}
```

**Key findings**:

-   **Hard vs. Easy**: Hard trials showed substantially lower accuracy than Easy ($\beta$ = -2.97, *p* \< .001). Easy trials had 85.2% accuracy, while Hard trials had 30.5% accuracy (well below chance). This reflects the increased difficulty of detecting small frequency/contrast differences on "different" trials, demonstrating a strong effect of stimulus difference magnitude on discrimination performance.
-   **High vs. Low Effort**: High effort (40% MVC) showed slightly lower accuracy than Low effort (5% MVC) ($\beta$ = -0.15, *p* = .001). Low effort had 58.5% accuracy, while High effort had 56.8% accuracy. This suggests that the increased physical effort required for High effort trials may interfere with cognitive performance, potentially due to dual-task resource competition between maintaining grip force and performing the discrimination task.

**RT (LMM on median RT):** Model: `rt_median ~ difficulty + effort + (1 | subject)`, restricted to Easy and Hard trials only (N = 13,771 trials, pooled across ADT and VDT). Reference levels: Easy, Low_5_MVC. Results are shown in @tbl-rt-lmm.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-rt-lmm
#| tbl-cap: "RT LMM Results"
if (!is.null(rt_lmm)) {
  # Function to clean up term names for publication (same as accuracy model, vectorized)
  clean_term_name <- function(term) {
    term <- as.character(term)
    
    # Intercept
    term <- ifelse(term == "(Intercept)", "Intercept", term)
    
    # Step 1: Handle interactions FIRST (on raw R terms)
    # Difficulty × Task interactions
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:taskVDT", "Difficulty: Easy × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:taskADT", "Difficulty: Easy × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:taskVDT", "Difficulty: Hard × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:taskADT", "Difficulty: Hard × Task: ADT", term)
    
    # Effort × Task interactions
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_5_MVC:taskVDT", "Effort: Low (5% MVC) × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_5_MVC:taskADT", "Effort: Low (5% MVC) × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC:taskVDT", "Effort: High (40% MVC) × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC:taskADT", "Effort: High (40% MVC) × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow:taskVDT", "Effort: Low × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionLow:taskADT", "Effort: Low × Task: ADT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh:taskVDT", "Effort: High × Task: VDT", term)
    term <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh:taskADT", "Effort: High × Task: ADT", term)
    
    # Difficulty × Effort interactions
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionLow_5_MVC", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: Low (5% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: High (40% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionLow_5_MVC", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: Low (5% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: High (40% MVC)", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionLow", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: Low", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy:effort_conditionHigh", "Difficulty: Easy × Effort: High", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionLow", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: Low", term)
    term <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard:effort_conditionHigh", "Difficulty: Hard × Effort: High", term)
    
    # Step 2: Handle main effects (only for terms NOT already processed as interactions)
    # Check if term is NOT already an interaction (doesn't contain ×)
    main_effect_mask <- !grepl(" × ", term)
    
    # Main effects (preserve colons - these separate factor name from level)
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("difficulty_levelEasy", "Difficulty: Easy", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("difficulty_levelHard", "Difficulty: Hard", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionLow_5_MVC", "Effort: Low", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh_MVC", "Effort: High", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionLow", "Effort: Low", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("effort_conditionHigh", "Effort: High", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("taskVDT", "Task: VDT", term[main_effect_mask])
    term[main_effect_mask] <- gsub("taskADT", "Task: ADT", term[main_effect_mask])
    
    # Step 3: For any remaining raw R interactions (not caught above), convert colon to ×
    # Only if term still has raw R format colons (between factor names, not in cleaned format)
    raw_interaction_mask <- grepl("_condition|_level|task", term) & grepl(":", term) & !grepl(" × ", term)
    term[raw_interaction_mask] <- gsub(":", " × ", term[raw_interaction_mask])
    
    return(term)
  }
  
  rt_lmm %>%
    filter(effect == "fixed") %>%
    mutate(
      term_clean = clean_term_name(term),
      estimate_fmt = sprintf("%.3f", estimate),
      ci_fmt = sprintf("[%.3f, %.3f]", conf.low, conf.high)
    ) %>%
    select(term_clean, estimate_fmt, std.error, statistic, ci_fmt) %>%
    rename(term = term_clean) %>%
    gt() %>%
    cols_label(
      term = "Term",
      estimate_fmt = "β (seconds)",
      std.error = "SE",
      ci_fmt = "95% CI"
    )
}
```

**Key findings**:

-   **Hard vs. Easy**: Hard trials were slower than Easy ($\beta$ = 0.23 s, 95% CI \[0.20, 0.27\]). Easy trials had a median RT of 0.75 s (mean 0.90 s), while Hard trials had a median RT of 1.01 s (mean 1.12 s). This reflects slower decision-making when stimulus differences are smaller and harder to detect.
-   **High vs. Low Effort**: High effort showed no significant difference in RT compared to Low effort ($\beta$ = 0.02 s, 95% CI \[-0.02, 0.05\]). Low effort had a median RT of 0.86 s (mean 1.00 s), while High effort had a median RT of 0.89 s (mean 1.02 s). The effort manipulation did not significantly affect reaction time, suggesting that the dual-task demands primarily affected accuracy rather than response speed.

**Conclusion**: Both experimental manipulations worked as intended. The **difficulty manipulation** (Easy vs. Hard within "different" trials) showed strong effects on both accuracy and RT in theoretically expected directions: larger stimulus differences (Easy) led to higher accuracy (85.2% vs. 30.5%) and faster RTs (0.75 s vs. 1.01 s median) compared to smaller differences (Hard). The **effort manipulation** (Low vs. High MVC) showed a small but significant effect on accuracy, with High effort slightly reducing accuracy (56.8% vs. 58.5%), likely due to dual-task resource competition. However, effort did not significantly affect RT. These results validate the experimental design prior to DDM analysis.

  }

    subj_col <- if ("subject_id" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "subject_id" else if ("sub" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "sub" else NULL
    
    if (!is.null(subj_col)) {
      # Subject-level accuracy by condition
      acc_by_condition <- behavioral_data %>%
        group_by(!!sym(task_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col), !!sym(subj_col)) %>%
        summarise(

            !!sym(diff_col) == "Hard" ~ "Hard",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(diff_col))
          ),
          Effort = case_when(

            !!sym(effort_col) == "low" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
            !!sym(effort_col) == "high" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(effort_col))
          )

    acc_table_data <- acc_by_condition %>%

        ),
        Difficulty = Difficulty,
        Effort = Effort,

      ) %>%
      select(Task_Group, Difficulty, Effort, `Mean %`, `SD %`, `Median %`, `Min %`, `Max %`, `N`)
    
    # Create gt table with row groups using groupname_col

      tab_options(

      )
    } else {
      # Placeholder if subject column not found

      cat("Subject ID column not found. Please ensure data contains: subject_id or sub\n")
    }
  } else {

  } else if ("accuracy" %in% names(behavioral_data)) {
    acc_col <- "accuracy"
  } else {
    acc_col <- NULL
  }
}

if (!is.null(behavioral_data) && !is.null(acc_col)) {
  subj_col <- if ("subject_id" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "subject_id" else if ("sub" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "sub" else NULL
  
  if (!is.null(subj_col)) {
    overall_acc <- behavioral_data %>%
      group_by(!!sym(subj_col)) %>%
      summarise(
        n_trials = n(),
        n_correct = sum(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE),
        accuracy = mean(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      )
  
    overall_summary <- overall_acc %>%
      summarise(
        n_subjects = n(),
        mean_acc = round(mean(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
        sd_acc = round(sd(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
        median_acc = round(median(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
        min_acc = round(min(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
        max_acc = round(max(accuracy, na.rm = TRUE) * 100, 1),
        total_trials = sum(n_trials)
      )
    
    overall_summary %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_label(
        n_subjects = "N Subjects",
        mean_acc = "Mean %",
        sd_acc = "SD %",
        median_acc = "Median %",
        min_acc = "Min %",
        max_acc = "Max %",
        total_trials = "Total Trials"
      ) %>%
      fmt_number(columns = c(mean_acc, sd_acc, median_acc, min_acc, max_acc), decimals = 1) %>%
      fmt_number(columns = c(n_subjects, total_trials), decimals = 0)
  } else {
    # Placeholder if subject column not found
    tibble(
      Metric = c("N Subjects", "Mean Accuracy", "SD", "Median", "Range"),
      Value = c(
        as.character(n_subj_final),
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed"
      )
    ) %>%
      gt()
  }
} else {
  # Placeholder
  tibble(
    Metric = c("N Subjects", "Mean Accuracy", "SD", "Median", "Range"),
    Value = c(
      as.character(n_subj_final),
      "To be computed",
      "To be computed",
      "To be computed",
      "To be computed"
    )
  ) %>%
    gt()
}

if (!is.null(behavioral_data)) {

  } else {

  }
  
  subj_col <- if ("subject_id" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "subject_id" else if ("sub" %in% names(behavioral_data)) "sub" else NULL
  
  if (!is.null(acc_col) && !is.null(task_col) && !is.null(diff_col) && !is.null(effort_col) && !is.null(subj_col)) {
    # Compute subject-level mean accuracy by condition
    acc_plot_data <- behavioral_data %>%

        mean_acc = mean(!!sym(acc_col), na.rm = TRUE) * 100,  # Convert to percentage
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(
        Task = case_when(
          !!sym(task_col) == "ADT" ~ "ADT",
          !!sym(task_col) == "VDT" ~ "VDT",

    if (!is.null(subj_col)) {
      # Global RT characteristics
      global_rt <- behavioral_data %>%
        filter(!is.na(!!sym(rt_col)), !!sym(rt_col) > 0) %>%
        summarise(
          n_trials = n(),
          mean_rt = round(mean(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          sd_rt = round(sd(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          median_rt = round(median(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          q25_rt = round(quantile(!!sym(rt_col), 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          q75_rt = round(quantile(!!sym(rt_col), 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          iqr_rt = round(q75_rt - q25_rt, 3),
          min_rt = round(min(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          max_rt = round(max(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE), 3)
        )
      
      # Condition-wise RT summary (subject-level medians)
      rt_by_condition <- behavioral_data %>%
        filter(!is.na(!!sym(rt_col)), !!sym(rt_col) > 0) %>%
        group_by(!!sym(task_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col), !!sym(subj_col)) %>%
        summarise(
          median_rt_subj = median(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE),
          mean_rt_subj = mean(!!sym(rt_col), na.rm = TRUE),
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        group_by(!!sym(task_col), !!sym(diff_col), !!sym(effort_col)) %>%
        summarise(
          mean_rt = round(mean(median_rt_subj, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          sd_rt = round(sd(median_rt_subj, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          median_rt = round(median(median_rt_subj, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          q25_rt = round(quantile(median_rt_subj, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          q75_rt = round(quantile(median_rt_subj, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
          iqr_rt = round(q75_rt - q25_rt, 3),
          n_subjects = n(),
          .groups = "drop"
        ) %>%
        # Clean up factor labels for display
        mutate(
          Task = case_when(
            !!sym(task_col) == "ADT" ~ "ADT",
            !!sym(task_col) == "VDT" ~ "VDT",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(task_col))
          ),
          Difficulty = case_when(
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Standard" ~ "Standard",
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Easy" ~ "Easy",
            !!sym(diff_col) == "Hard" ~ "Hard",
            TRUE ~ as.character(!!sym(diff_col))
          ),
          Effort = case_when(
            !!sym(effort_col) == "Low_5_MVC" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",

        transmute(
          `N Trials` = n_trials,

          `SD (s)` = sd_rt,
          `Median (s)` = median_rt,
          `IQR (s)` = iqr_rt,
          `Min (s)` = min_rt,
          `Max (s)` = max_rt
        ) %>%
        gt() %>%
        fmt_number(columns = where(is.numeric) & !matches("N Trials"), decimals = 3) %>%
        fmt_number(columns = matches("N Trials"), decimals = 0)
    } else {
      cat("**RT Descriptives**:\n")
      cat("Subject ID column not found. Please ensure data contains: subject_id or sub\n")
    }

    cat("RT column not identified. Please ensure data contains: rt/resp1RT/RT column\n")
  }

**Summary**: As shown in @fig-rt-distribution, reaction times were strongly right-skewed, with most responses occurring in the 0.5-1.5 s range. Easy trials showed faster RTs (peaks shifted left) compared to Hard trials (peaks shifted right), consistent with the difficulty manipulation. Effort effects on RT were minimal compared to difficulty effects, suggesting that the dual-task demands primarily affected accuracy rather than response speed.

## RT definition: cue-locked vs probe-onset-locked

We evaluated two RT definitions for the DDM analysis. **Cue-locked RT** is measured from response-window onset (when the response signal appears). **Probe-onset-locked RT** is measured from probe stimulus onset, incorporating the fixed delays before the response window (probe duration plus GripRelaxTime) plus the response-window RT component.

```{r}
#| label: fig-rt-distributions
#| fig-cap: "RT distributions for cue-locked vs probe-onset-locked definitions. Histograms show the distribution of response times for each RT definition across all trials. Cue-locked RTs are measured from response-window onset, while probe-onset-locked RTs incorporate the fixed delays before the response window (probe duration + GripRelaxTime ≈ 0.35s) plus the response-window RT component. The probe-onset-locked distribution is shifted rightward by approximately 0.35s relative to cue-locked, reflecting the additional time from probe onset to response-window onset."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "90%"
library(ggplot2)

# Read unthresholded data for RT distributions
rt_data_file <- file.path(params$run_dir, "ddm_ready_data_unthresholded.csv")
if (file.exists(rt_data_file)) {
  rt_data <- read_csv(rt_data_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
  
  # Create RT definition column
  rt_plot_data <- rt_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(rt_cue_locked), !is.na(rt_probe_onset_locked)) %>%
    mutate(
      cue_locked = rt_cue_locked,
      probe_onset_locked = rt_probe_onset_locked
    ) %>%
    select(cue_locked, probe_onset_locked) %>%
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "rt_type", values_to = "rt") %>%
    mutate(
      rt_type = case_when(
        rt_type == "cue_locked" ~ "Cue-locked RT",
        rt_type == "probe_onset_locked" ~ "Probe-onset-locked RT",
        TRUE ~ rt_type
      )
    ) %>%
    filter(rt > 0, rt < 5)  # Reasonable RT range for visualization
  
  p_rt_dist <- ggplot(rt_plot_data, aes(x = rt, fill = rt_type)) +
    geom_histogram(alpha = 0.6, bins = 50, position = "identity") +
    facet_wrap(~rt_type, ncol = 1) +
    labs(
      x = "Response Time (s)",
      y = "Frequency",
      fill = "RT Definition"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      legend.position = "none",
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
    )
  
  print(p_rt_dist)
} else {
  cat("RT distribution data not available.")
}
```

This RT definition choice connects directly to the experimental design:

- Participants can begin evidence accumulation at probe onset, as the probe stimulus contains the task-relevant information.
- Motor execution may be gated until the response window, as participants must wait for the response signal before making their button press.
- Therefore, probe-onset-locked RT yields a non-decision time scale interpretable relative to decision onset (probe), allowing clearer separation of evidence accumulation time from motor execution and response gating delays.

Model comparison metrics between RT definitions are not decisive on their own; design logic motivates selecting probe-onset-locked as the primary RT definition.

## Model comparison (baseline vs additive; cue vs probe-onset)

```{r}
#| label: tbl-loo-comparison
#| tbl-cap: "LOO model comparison for baseline vs additive models across RT definitions (threshold = 0.20 s)."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
# Build LOO comparison table (using standardized column names)
# First ensure optional columns exist
tbl_loo_comp_base <- loo_summary %>%
  filter(threshold == PRIMARY_THR)
if (!"looic_se" %in% names(tbl_loo_comp_base)) {
  tbl_loo_comp_base <- tbl_loo_comp_base %>% mutate(looic_se = NA_real_)
}
if (!"elpd_loo" %in% names(tbl_loo_comp_base)) {
  tbl_loo_comp_base <- tbl_loo_comp_base %>% mutate(elpd_loo = NA_real_)
}
if (!"elpd_se" %in% names(tbl_loo_comp_base)) {
  tbl_loo_comp_base <- tbl_loo_comp_base %>% mutate(elpd_se = NA_real_)
}

tbl_loo_comp_raw <- tbl_loo_comp_base %>%
  select(model, rt_type, looic, looic_se, elpd_loo, elpd_se) %>%
  mutate(
    delta_looic = looic - min(looic, na.rm = TRUE)
  )

# Extract values for inline text before rounding/renaming
baseline_min_delta <- tbl_loo_comp_raw %>%
  filter(model == "baseline") %>%
  pull(delta_looic) %>%
  min(na.rm = TRUE)
additive_max_delta <- tbl_loo_comp_raw %>%
  filter(model == PRIMARY_MODEL) %>%
  pull(delta_looic) %>%
  max(na.rm = TRUE) %>%
  abs()

# Create display table with rounded values and renamed columns
tbl_loo_comp <- tbl_loo_comp_raw %>%
  mutate(
    looic = round(looic, 1),
    looic_se = round(looic_se, 1),
    delta_looic = round(delta_looic, 1),
    elpd_loo = round(elpd_loo, 1),
    elpd_se = round(elpd_se, 1)
  ) %>%
  arrange(delta_looic) %>%
  rename(
    `Model` = model,
    `RT definition` = rt_type,
    `LOOIC` = looic,
    `LOOIC SE` = looic_se,
    `Δ LOOIC` = delta_looic,
    `ELPD LOO` = elpd_loo,
    `ELPD SE` = elpd_se
  )

# Render table
tbl_loo_comp %>%
  knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), 
               booktabs = TRUE, 
               linesep = "") %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"),
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE
  )
```

The additive model strongly outperforms the baseline model, with Δ LOOIC values of `r round(baseline_min_delta, 1)` or more relative to the best-fitting additive model. Differences between cue-locked and probe-onset-locked RT definitions are minimal (Δ LOOIC < `r round(additive_max_delta, 1)`, within standard error), indicating that model fit is not decisive for RT definition selection. Therefore, the choice of probe-onset-locked RT as primary is motivated by design logic rather than model comparison metrics.

```{r}
#| label: fig-loo-comparison
#| fig-cap: "LOO model comparison: baseline vs additive models across RT definitions. Points show LOOIC values with error bars indicating standard errors. Lower LOOIC indicates better predictive performance. The additive model (circles) strongly outperforms the baseline model (triangles) for both RT definitions. Differences between cue-locked (blue) and probe-onset-locked (red) RT definitions are minimal within each model, supporting the design-based choice of probe-onset-locked RT as primary."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "70%"
library(ggplot2)

loo_plot_data <- loo_summary %>%
  filter(threshold == PRIMARY_THR) %>%
  mutate(
    model_label = case_when(
      model == "baseline" ~ "Baseline",
      model == "additive" ~ "Additive",
      TRUE ~ model
    ),
    rt_label = case_when(
      rt_type == "cue_locked" ~ "Cue-locked",
      rt_type == "probe_onset_locked" ~ "Probe-onset-locked",
      TRUE ~ rt_type
    )
  )

p_loo <- ggplot(loo_plot_data, aes(x = model_label, y = looic, color = rt_label, shape = model_label)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = looic - looic_se, ymax = looic + looic_se), 
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), size = 0.8) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Cue-locked" = "#2E86AB", "Probe-onset-locked" = "#A23B72"), name = "RT Definition") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("Baseline" = 17, "Additive" = 19), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    x = "Model",
    y = "LOOIC (lower is better)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom"
  )

print(p_loo)
```

## Behavioral DDM parameter estimates (no pupil)

The following parameter estimates are from the primary behavioral model (`r PRIMARY_MODEL` model, threshold `r PRIMARY_THR` s, `r PRIMARY_RT` RT definition). We use response-side coding where the upper boundary corresponds to "different" responses and the lower boundary corresponds to "same" responses. Starting-point bias (z) is interpreted relative to 0.5: values above 0.5 indicate a bias toward "different" responses (upper boundary), while values below 0.5 indicate a bias toward "same" responses (lower boundary).

**Note on table structure**: By model specification, drift rate (v), boundary separation (a), and non-decision time (t₀) do not vary by task—only by difficulty and effort. Starting-point bias (z) varies by task and effort but is constrained to be constant across difficulty levels (as trials are randomized). Therefore, we present these parameters in separate tables optimized for their respective structures.

**Note on precision**: Credible intervals are shown on the link scale; values are reported to 3 decimals to avoid apparent repetition due to rounding.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-ddm-core-by-difficulty-effort
#| tbl-cap: "Core DDM parameters (v, a, t₀) by Difficulty × Effort. Task does not vary for these parameters by model specification. Values are posterior medians with 95% credible intervals."
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
# Table A: v/a/t0 by Difficulty × Effort (collapse across task since values are identical)
ddm_core <- pred_params %>%
  filter(model == PRIMARY_MODEL, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT, threshold == PRIMARY_THR) %>%
  group_by(difficulty, effort) %>%
  slice(1) %>%  # Take first task per difficulty×effort (values are identical by design)
  ungroup() %>%
  select(difficulty, effort, 
         drift_median, drift_q2.5, drift_q97.5,
         a_median, a_q2.5, a_q97.5,
         t0_median, t0_q2.5, t0_q97.5) %>%
  mutate(
    difficulty = factor(difficulty, levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard")),
    effort = factor(effort, levels = c("Low", "High"))
  ) %>%
  arrange(difficulty, effort) %>%
  mutate(
    `Drift (v)` = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", drift_median, drift_q2.5, drift_q97.5),
    `Boundary (a)` = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", a_median, a_q2.5, a_q97.5),
    `Non-decision (t₀)` = sprintf("%.3f [%.3f, %.3f]", t0_median, t0_q2.5, t0_q97.5)
  ) %>%
  select(Difficulty = difficulty, Effort = effort, `Drift (v)`, `Boundary (a)`, `Non-decision (t₀)`)

message(sprintf("ddm_core table: %d rows (should be %d difficulty × %d effort = %d)", 
                nrow(ddm_core), 
                length(unique(pred_params$difficulty)), 
                length(unique(pred_params$effort)),
                length(unique(pred_params$difficulty)) * length(unique(pred_params$effort))))

ddm_core %>%
  knitr::kable(format = ifelse(knitr::is_latex_output(), "latex", "html"), 
               booktabs = TRUE, 
               linesep = "",
               align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r")) %>%
  kableExtra::kable_styling(
    latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"),
    bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed", "responsive"),
    full_width = FALSE
  )
```

    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = bias_lower, ymax = bias_upper), 
                    position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), size = 0.6) +
    facet_grid(task ~ difficulty, labeller = labeller(task = c("ADT" = "ADT", "VDT" = "VDT"),
                                                      difficulty = c("Standard" = "Standard", "Easy" = "Easy", "Hard" = "Hard"))) +
    labs(
      x = "Effort Condition",
      y = "Starting-Point Bias (z)",
      title = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA)
    )
} else {
  # If no difficulty column, facet only by task (bias is constant across difficulty by design)
  p_bias_std <- ggplot(bias_std_plot_data, aes(x = effort_label, y = bias_val)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey50", alpha = 0.5) +
    geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = bias_lower, ymax = bias_upper), 
                    position = position_dodge(width = 0.3), size = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~ task, labeller = labeller(task = c("ADT" = "ADT", "VDT" = "VDT"))) +
    labs(
      x = "Effort Condition",
      y = "Starting-Point Bias (z)",
      title = NULL
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA)
    )
}

print(p_bias_std)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-all-parameters-summary
#| fig-cap: "Posterior predicted parameters by task × effort × difficulty (primary spec: probe-onset-locked RT, 0.20s cutoff). Points show posterior medians with 95% credible intervals (error bars). Parameters are faceted: Drift (v) measures evidence accumulation rate; Boundary (a/bs) measures decision threshold; Non-decision time (ndt/t₀) measures encoding and motor execution time; Starting point (z) measures response bias. Effort conditions are color-coded (Low = blue, High = red), and task is indicated by shape (ADT = circle, VDT = triangle)."
#| fig-align: center
#| out-width: "90%"
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)

# Prepare data: filter to primary model and long-format all parameters (using standardized column names)
params_base <- pred_params %>%
  filter(model == PRIMARY_MODEL, rt_type == PRIMARY_RT, threshold == PRIMARY_THR) %>%
  select(task, effort, difficulty, 
         drift_median, drift_q2.5, drift_q97.5,
         a_median, a_q2.5, a_q97.5,
         t0_median, t0_q2.5, t0_q97.5,
         z_median, z_q2.5, z_q97.5) %>%
  mutate(
    difficulty = factor(difficulty, levels = c("Standard", "Easy", "Hard")),
    effort = factor(effort, levels = c("Low", "High")),
    task = factor(task, levels = c("ADT", "VDT"))
  )

# Create long format by binding rows for each parameter
params_long <- bind_rows(
  params_base %>% 
    select(task, effort, difficulty, median = drift_median, q2.5 = drift_q2.5, q97.5 = drift_q97.5) %>%
    mutate(parameter = "Drift (v)"),
  params_base %>% 
    select(task, effort, difficulty, median = a_median, q2.5 = a_q2.5, q97.5 = a_q97.5) %>%
    mutate(parameter = "Boundary (a)"),
  params_base %>% 
    select(task, effort, difficulty, median = t0_median, q2.5 = t0_q2.5, q97.5 = t0_q97.5) %>%
    mutate(parameter = "Non-decision time (ndt)"),
  params_base %>% 
    select(task, effort, difficulty, median = z_median, q2.5 = z_q2.5, q97.5 = z_q97.5) %>%
    mutate(parameter = "Starting point (z)")
) %>%
  mutate(
    parameter = factor(parameter, levels = c("Drift (v)", "Boundary (a)", "Non-decision time (ndt)", "Starting point (z)"))
  )

# Create plot
p_all_params <- ggplot(params_long, aes(x = difficulty, y = median, color = effort, shape = task, group = interaction(effort, task))) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = q2.5, ymax = q97.5), 
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.4), size = 0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~ parameter, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Low" = "#5DADE2", "High" = "#A23B72"), name = "Effort") +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("ADT" = 19, "VDT" = 17), name = "Task") +
  labs(
    x = "Difficulty",
    y = "Parameter Value",
    title = NULL
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    strip.text = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA)
  )

print(p_all_params)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
# Extract values for narrative interpretation
drift_high_easy <- pred_params %>% filter(effort == "High", difficulty == "Easy") %>% pull(drift_median) %>% first()
drift_low_easy <- pred_params %>% filter(effort == "Low", difficulty == "Easy") %>% pull(drift_median) %>% first()
a_high_mean <- pred_params %>% filter(effort == "High") %>% pull(a_median) %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
a_low_mean <- pred_params %>% filter(effort == "Low") %>% pull(a_median) %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
t0_mean <- mean(pred_params$t0_median, na.rm = TRUE)
t0_min <- min(pred_params$t0_q2.5, na.rm = TRUE)
t0_max <- max(pred_params$t0_q97.5, na.rm = TRUE)
z_mean <- mean(pred_params$z_median, na.rm = TRUE)
z_vdt_mean <- pred_params %>% filter(task == "VDT") %>% pull(z_median) %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
z_adt_mean <- pred_params %>% filter(task == "ADT") %>% pull(z_median) %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
z_high_mean <- pred_params %>% filter(effort == "High") %>% pull(z_median) %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
z_low_mean <- pred_params %>% filter(effort == "Low") %>% pull(z_median) %>% mean(na.rm = TRUE)
```

**Drift rate (v)**: Easy trials show substantially higher drift rates than Hard trials across all conditions, with credible intervals indicating faster evidence accumulation for easier discriminations. `r if (!is.na(drift_high_easy) && !is.na(drift_low_easy)) { if (drift_high_easy < drift_low_easy) { "High effort shows lower drift rates than low effort, with credible intervals indicating reduced evidence accumulation under high effort." } else if (drift_high_easy > drift_low_easy) { "High effort shows higher drift rates than low effort, though credible intervals may overlap." } else { "Effort effects on drift rate are minimal, with credible intervals overlapping across effort conditions." } } else { "Effort effects on drift rate are minimal, with credible intervals overlapping across effort conditions." }`

**Boundary separation (a)**: `r if (!is.na(a_high_mean) && !is.na(a_low_mean)) { if (a_high_mean > a_low_mean) { "High effort increases boundary separation relative to low effort, indicating increased caution under high effort." } else if (a_high_mean < a_low_mean) { "High effort decreases boundary separation relative to low effort, indicating reduced caution under high effort." } else { "Effort effects on boundary separation are minimal, with credible intervals overlapping across effort conditions." } } else { "Effort effects on boundary separation are minimal, with credible intervals overlapping across effort conditions." }`

**Non-decision time (t₀)**: Non-decision time values are approximately `r round(t0_mean, 2)` s (median across conditions), with credible intervals spanning `r round(t0_min, 2)` to `r round(t0_max, 2)` s. These values reflect the probe-onset-locked time base and should not be overinterpreted.

**Starting-point bias (z)**: `r if (!is.na(z_mean)) { if (z_mean > 0.5) { paste0("Overall bias is above 0.5 (median = ", round(z_mean, 3), "), indicating a bias toward 'different' responses.") } else if (z_mean < 0.5) { paste0("Overall bias is below 0.5 (median = ", round(z_mean, 3), "), indicating a bias toward 'same' responses.") } else { "Overall bias is approximately 0.5, indicating no strong directional bias." } }` `r if (!is.na(z_vdt_mean) && !is.na(z_adt_mean) && abs(z_vdt_mean - z_adt_mean) > 0.01) { paste0("Task differences are present, with ", ifelse(z_vdt_mean < z_adt_mean, "VDT showing less bias toward 'different' than ADT", "VDT showing more bias toward 'different' than ADT"), ".") }` `r if (!is.na(z_high_mean) && !is.na(z_low_mean) && abs(z_high_mean - z_low_mean) > 0.01) { paste0("Effort effects on bias are present, with ", ifelse(z_high_mean > z_low_mean, "high effort increasing bias toward 'different'", "high effort decreasing bias toward 'different'"), ".") }`

### Fixed Effects Overview

The primary model estimated fixed effects for all DDM parameters across difficulty, task, and effort conditions. @fig-fixed-effects-adt and @fig-fixed-effects-vdt show forest plots of fixed effects by task.

```{r tbl-pupil-quality-summary}
#| echo: false
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| tbl-cap: "Pupil Data Quality Summary"
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
if (!exists("pupil_data") || is.null(pupil_data) || nrow(pupil_data) == 0) {
  cat("Pupil data not loaded; skipping pupil quality summary.\n")
} else {
  library(dplyr)
  library(rlang)
  library(gt)
  
  # Count subjects with usable pupil data
  if ("subject_id" %in% names(pupil_data)) {
    n_subj_pupil <- length(unique(pupil_data$subject_id))
  } else {
    n_subj_pupil <- 0L
  }
  
  # Find quality column (look for common quality/rejection column names)
  quality_col <- NULL
  quality_candidates <- c("quality", "rejection", "valid_samples", "pupil_quality", "sample_quality")
  for (col in quality_candidates) {
    if (col %in% names(pupil_data)) {
      quality_col <- col
      break
    }
  }
  
  # Compute quality metrics if quality column exists
  if (!is.null(quality_col) && quality_col %in% names(pupil_data)) {
    # Use rlang::sym for dynamic column access
    quality_var <- sym(quality_col)
    
    # Trial-level quality
    mean_quality_trial <- mean(pupil_data[[quality_col]], na.rm = TRUE) * 100
    sd_quality_trial <- sd(pupil_data[[quality_col]], na.rm = TRUE) * 100
    
    # Subject-level quality
    subj_quality <- pupil_data %>%
      group_by(subject_id) %>%
      summarise(mean_quality = mean(!!quality_var, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")
    mean_quality_subj <- mean(subj_quality$mean_quality, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  } else {
    mean_quality_trial <- NA_real_
    sd_quality_trial <- NA_real_
    mean_quality_subj <- NA_real_
  }
  
  # Count trials
  n_trials_total <- nrow(pupil_data)
  
  # Compute trials per condition (if difficulty_level and effort_condition are available)
  if ("difficulty_level" %in% names(pupil_data) && "effort_condition" %in% names(pupil_data) && "task" %in% names(pupil_data)) {
    trials_per_condition <- pupil_data %>%
      filter(!is.na(difficulty_level), !is.na(effort_condition)) %>%
      group_by(task, difficulty_level, effort_condition) %>%
      summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
      summarise(mean_n = mean(n))
    mean_trials_per_condition <- round(trials_per_condition$mean_n, 1)
  } else {
    mean_trials_per_condition <- NA_real_
  }
  
  # Create table
  pupil_quality_table <- tibble(
    Metric = c(
      "Subjects with usable pupil data",
      "Total trials with pupil data",
      if (!is.na(mean_quality_trial)) "Mean % valid samples per trial",
      if (!is.na(sd_quality_trial)) "SD % valid samples per trial",
      if (!is.na(mean_quality_subj)) "Mean % valid samples per subject",
      if (!is.na(mean_trials_per_condition)) "Mean valid trials per condition"
    ),
    Value = c(
      as.character(n_subj_pupil),
      format(n_trials_total, big.mark = ","),
      if (!is.na(mean_quality_trial)) sprintf("%.1f%%", mean_quality_trial),
      if (!is.na(sd_quality_trial)) sprintf("%.1f%%", sd_quality_trial),
      if (!is.na(mean_quality_subj)) sprintf("%.1f%%", mean_quality_subj),
      if (!is.na(mean_trials_per_condition)) as.character(mean_trials_per_condition)
    )
  )
  
  # Only create table if we have meaningful data
  if (n_subj_pupil > 0 && n_trials_total > 0) {
    pupil_quality_table %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_label(
        Metric = "Metric",
        Value = "Value"
      )
  } else {
    # Placeholder if data exists but is empty
    pupil_quality_placeholder <- tibble(
      Metric = c(
        "Subjects with usable pupil data",
        "Mean % valid samples per trial",
        "SD % valid samples per trial",
        "Mean % valid samples per subject",
        "Trials excluded (pupil artifacts)",
        "Mean valid trials per condition"
      ),
      Value = c(
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed",
        "To be computed"
      )
    )
    
    pupil_quality_placeholder %>%
      gt() %>%
      cols_label(
        Metric = "Metric",
        Value = "Value"
      ) %>%
      tab_footnote(
        footnote = "Pupil data file not found or empty. Please ensure ch3_triallevel.csv is available in quick_share_v7/analysis_ready/",
        locations = cells_body()
      )
  }
}
```

Baseline pupil diameter by condition is shown in @tbl-baseline-pupil.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-baseline-pupil
#| tbl-cap: "Baseline Pupil Diameter by Condition"
#| tbl-pos: "htbp"
# Compute baseline pupil diameter by task and effort
if (!is.null(pupil_data) && "baseline_B0" %in% names(pupil_data) && "task" %in% names(pupil_data) && "effort_condition" %in% names(pupil_data)) {
  baseline_pupil_summary <- pupil_data %>%
    filter(!is.na(baseline_B0), !is.na(task), !is.na(effort_condition)) %>%
    group_by(task, effort_condition, subject_id) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_baseline = mean(baseline_B0, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    group_by(task, effort_condition) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_baseline_mm = round(mean(mean_baseline, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      sd_baseline_mm = round(sd(mean_baseline, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      median_baseline_mm = round(median(mean_baseline, na.rm = TRUE), 2),
      n_subjects = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      Task_Group = case_when(
        task == "ADT" ~ "ADT (Auditory Detection Task)",
        task == "VDT" ~ "VDT (Visual Detection Task)",
        TRUE ~ task
      ),
      Effort = case_when(
        effort_condition == "Low_5_MVC" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
        effort_condition == "High_40_MVC" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
        TRUE ~ effort_condition
      ),
      `Mean (mm)` = mean_baseline_mm,
      `SD (mm)` = sd_baseline_mm,
      `Median (mm)` = median_baseline_mm,
      `N Subjects` = n_subjects
    ) %>%
    arrange(Task_Group, Effort) %>%
    select(Task_Group, Effort, `Mean (mm)`, `SD (mm)`, `Median (mm)`, `N Subjects`)
  
  baseline_pupil_summary %>%
    gt(groupname_col = "Task_Group") %>%
    fmt_number(columns = c(`Mean (mm)`, `SD (mm)`, `Median (mm)`), decimals = 2) %>%
    fmt_number(columns = `N Subjects`, decimals = 0) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_column_labels()
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold", style = "italic"),
      locations = cells_row_groups()
    ) %>%
    tab_options(
      row_group.as_column = FALSE,
      row_group.padding = px(8)
    ) %>%
    tab_footnote(
      footnote = "Baseline pupil diameter (tonic arousal) computed from pre-trial baseline window (-0.5s to 0s relative to squeeze onset).",
      locations = cells_column_labels(columns = `Mean (mm)`)
    )
} else {
  # Placeholder if data not available
  baseline_pupil_placeholder <- expand_grid(
    task = c("ADT", "VDT"),
    effort_condition = c("Low_5_MVC", "High_40_MVC")
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      Task_Group = case_when(
        task == "ADT" ~ "ADT (Auditory Detection Task)",
        task == "VDT" ~ "VDT (Visual Detection Task)",
        TRUE ~ task
      ),
      Effort = case_when(
        effort_condition == "Low_5_MVC" ~ "Low (5% MVC)",
        effort_condition == "High_40_MVC" ~ "High (40% MVC)",
        TRUE ~ effort_condition
      ),
      `Mean (mm)` = "To be computed",
      `SD (mm)` = "To be computed",
      `Median (mm)` = "To be computed",
      `N Subjects` = "To be computed"
    ) %>%
    arrange(Task_Group, Effort) %>%
    select(Task_Group, Effort, `Mean (mm)`, `SD (mm)`, `Median (mm)`, `N Subjects`)
  
  baseline_pupil_placeholder %>%
    gt(groupname_col = "Task_Group") %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold"),
      locations = cells_column_labels()
    ) %>%
    tab_style(
      style = cell_text(weight = "bold", style = "italic"),
      locations = cells_row_groups()
    ) %>%
    tab_options(
      row_group.as_column = FALSE,
      row_group.padding = px(8)
    ) %>%
    tab_footnote(
      footnote = "Baseline pupil data not available. Please ensure pupil data file contains baseline_B0 column.",
      locations = cells_body()
    )
}

      footnote = "TEPR data not available. Please ensure pupil data file contains cognitive_auc, task, effort_condition, and difficulty_level columns.",
      locations = cells_body()
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-tepr-timecourse
#| fig-cap: "Task-Evoked Pupil Response (TEPR) Time Course. Grand-average pupil traces (baseline-corrected, mean ± 95% CI) aligned to squeeze onset for four conditions (Easy/Low, Easy/High, Hard/Low, Hard/High), separately for ADT (top) and VDT (bottom). The shaded region indicates the cognitive AUC window used for TEPR quantification (4.65s to 7.65s relative to squeeze onset, extending from 300ms after target stimulus onset until ~3s post-target). Baseline-corrected traces converge at 0 during the baseline period (-0.5 to 0s). Vertical dashed lines indicate key events: trial start (0s), target stimulus onset (4.35s), and response signal onset (4.7s)."
#| fig-align: center
#| echo: false
# Generate TEPR time course figure
if (!is.null(pupil_data)) {
  # Try to load waveform summary data
  waveform_file <- file.path(proj_root, "quick_share_v7/analysis/pupil_waveforms_condition_mean.csv")
  
  if (file.exists(waveform_file)) {
    waveform_data <- read_csv(waveform_file, show_col_types = FALSE)
    
    # Filter to chapter 3 data and keep all 4 conditions (effort × difficulty)
    waveform_ch3 <- waveform_data %>%
      filter(chapter == "ch3") %>%
      # Map difficulty level from stimulus_intensity and isOddball
      mutate(
        difficulty_level = case_when(
          isOddball == 0 | (is.na(isOddball) & (!is.na(stimulus_intensity) & stimulus_intensity == 0)) ~ "Standard",
          !is.na(stimulus_intensity) & stimulus_intensity %in% c(1, 2) ~ "Hard",
          !is.na(stimulus_intensity) & stimulus_intensity %in% c(3, 4) ~ "Easy",
          isOddball == 1 & is.na(stimulus_intensity) ~ "Easy",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        effort_level = case_when(
          effort == "Low" | effort == "Low_Force_5pct" ~ "Low",
          effort == "High" | effort == "High_Force_40pct" ~ "High",
          TRUE ~ NA_character_
        ),
        # Create condition label (Difficulty / Effort)
        condition = case_when(
          !is.na(difficulty_level) & !is.na(effort_level) ~ 
            paste0(difficulty_level, " / ", effort_level),
          TRUE ~ "Unknown"
        )
      ) %>%
      # Filter out Standard trials (we want Easy/Hard only) and Unknown
      filter(condition != "Unknown", !grepl("Standard", condition)) %>%
      # Use mean_pupil_full (baseline-corrected, B0-corrected) - this converges at 0 in baseline period
      # Per plot_pupil_waveforms.R line 134: mean_pupil_full is the B0-corrected (full baseline correction)
      rename(mean_pupil_isolated = mean_pupil_full) %>%
      # Group by task, condition, and time to get per-condition means
      group_by(task, condition, t_rel) %>%
      summarise(
        # Weighted mean across any duplicate entries (weight by n_trials)
        total_trials = sum(n_trials, na.rm = TRUE),
        mean_pupil_isolated = sum(mean_pupil_isolated * n_trials, na.rm = TRUE) / total_trials,
        n_trials = total_trials,
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      filter(!is.na(task), !is.na(condition), !is.na(t_rel), !is.na(mean_pupil_isolated)) %>%
      arrange(task, condition, t_rel)
    
    if (nrow(waveform_ch3) > 0) {
      # Define event markers and cognitive AUC window
      # Based on Methods section: cognitive AUC window is 4.65s to 7.65s (300ms after target until 3.3s post-target)
      trial_start <- 0.0  # Trial start (squeeze onset)
      target_onset <- 4.35  # Target stimulus onset
      response_signal_onset <- 4.7  # Response signal onset
      cognitive_auc_start <- 4.65  # 300ms after target onset (4.35 + 0.3)
      cognitive_auc_end <- 7.65  # 3.3s post-target (4.35 + 3.3), which is the W3.0 window
      
      # Define color scheme for 4 conditions (matching plot_pupil_waveforms.R)
      condition_colors <- c(
        "Easy / Low" = "#5DADE2",    # Light blue
        "Easy / High" = "#2E86AB",   # Dark blue  
        "Hard / Low" = "#EC70AB",    # Light pink
        "Hard / High" = "#A23B72"    # Dark pink
      )
      
      # Get conditions actually present in data
      conditions_present <- unique(waveform_ch3$condition)
      conditions_present <- conditions_present[!is.na(conditions_present)]
      colors_for_plot <- condition_colors[names(condition_colors) %in% conditions_present]
      if (length(colors_for_plot) == 0) {
        # Fallback: use default colors if no matches
        colors_for_plot <- scales::hue_pal()(length(conditions_present))
        names(colors_for_plot) <- conditions_present
      }
      
      # Calculate y-limits from data (use full range to show all curves, add padding for labels)
      y_vals <- waveform_ch3$mean_pupil_isolated[!is.na(waveform_ch3$mean_pupil_isolated)]
      if (length(y_vals) > 0) {
        # Use full range to ensure all curves are visible
        y_range <- range(y_vals, na.rm = TRUE)
        y_range_span <- diff(y_range)
        if (!is.finite(y_range_span) || y_range_span == 0) {
          y_range_span <- max(abs(y_range), na.rm = TRUE)
          if (!is.finite(y_range_span) || y_range_span == 0) y_range_span <- 1
        }
        # Add padding (12% top, 8% bottom) to accommodate labels and ensure visibility
        y_upper_limit <- y_range[2] + y_range_span * 0.12  # Extra space for labels
        y_lower_limit <- y_range[1] - y_range_span * 0.08  # Padding at bottom
      } else {
        y_upper_limit <- 0.5
        y_lower_limit <- -0.5
        y_range_span <- 1  # Default span for label positioning
      }
      
      # Event markers with staggered y positions to avoid overlap (vertical text)
      event_markers <- tibble(
        event = c("Trial Start", "Target", "Response"),
        time = c(trial_start, target_onset, response_signal_onset),
        label_y = y_upper_limit - y_range_span * c(0.05, 0.10, 0.15)  # Stagger vertically
      )
      
      # Create plot
      p_tepr <- ggplot(waveform_ch3, aes(x = t_rel, y = mean_pupil_isolated, 
                                         color = condition, fill = condition)) +
        # Cognitive AUC window shading
        geom_rect(aes(xmin = cognitive_auc_start, xmax = cognitive_auc_end, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, fill = "grey90", alpha = 0.3) +
        # GAM smoothed lines with confidence intervals
        geom_smooth(se = TRUE, method = "gam", formula = y ~ s(x, k = 20), 
                    linewidth = 1.2, alpha = 0.3) +
        # Event markers (vertical dashed lines)
        geom_vline(data = event_markers, aes(xintercept = time), 
                   inherit.aes = FALSE, linetype = "dashed", color = "grey40", linewidth = 0.6) +
        # Event labels (vertical text to avoid overlap)
        geom_text(data = event_markers, aes(x = time, y = label_y, label = event),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.9,
                  size = 3.5, color = "grey20", fontface = "bold") +
        # Facet by task (stacked vertically)
        facet_wrap(~task, ncol = 1, labeller = labeller(task = c("ADT" = "ADT (Auditory Detection Task)", 
                                                                  "VDT" = "VDT (Visual Detection Task)"))) +
        # Scales
        scale_color_manual(values = colors_for_plot, name = "Condition") +
        scale_fill_manual(values = colors_for_plot, name = "Condition") +
        scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(-0.5, 8, 1), expand = c(0, 0.1)) +
        coord_cartesian(ylim = c(y_lower_limit, y_upper_limit)) +
        # Labels and theme
        labs(
          x = "Time (s, relative to squeeze onset)",
          y = "Baseline-Corrected Pupil Diameter (mm)",
          title = NULL
        ) +
        theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
        theme(
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.5),
          strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
          strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", color = NA),
          legend.position = "bottom",
          legend.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          axis.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
          plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
        )
      
      # Print plot
      print(p_tepr)
    } else {
      # Placeholder if no data
      # Waveform data not available - ensure label still resolves
      invisible(NULL)
    }
  } else {
    # Placeholder if file not found
    # Waveform file not found - ensure label still resolves
    invisible(NULL)
  }
} else {
  # Placeholder if pupil_data not loaded - use invisible output to ensure label resolves
  invisible(NULL)
}
